![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14230052/assets/624bb949d80c1da50cba951b00210a2a26aeb3c44d77d4c2eed69c8e3ba0f4d4.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the path along the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4},$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to arc length over $C$ is equal to the arc length $L$ of $C,$ i.e.,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=L.
$$

In polar coordinates, the arc length element $\text{d}s$ is given by

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

So, for a polar curve defined as $r=r(\theta )$ for ${\theta }_{1}\le \theta \le {\theta }_{2},$ we have

$$
L={\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, we evaluate our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +9{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{9}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\text{d}\theta  \\  & =3\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =3(\frac{\pi }{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
